info1.title: The 50/30/20 rule
info1.body:
A simple way to split your take-home pay — the money that actually lands in your account after tax. Half goes to needs, a third to wants, and the rest to your future: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt.

Needs are the things you can't skip — rent, food, bills, getting to work. Wants are the nice-to-haves like eating out, subscriptions, or a weekend away. The last 20% is what quietly builds your safety net.

Best of all, there's no spreadsheet and no tracking every coffee. You just keep each bucket roughly in its lane, and the budget mostly takes care of itself.

q1.prompt: In the 50/30/20 rule, what does the 50% cover?
q1.explanation: The 50% slice covers essentials: housing, groceries, utilities and transport.

info2.title: Why the 20% matters most
info2.body:
That 20% is the slice most people cut first — and it's the one that changes everything. It's how you cover a surprise bill without reaching for a credit card, and how you clear debt that's quietly charging you interest every month.

The trick is to pay yourself first: set up an automatic transfer on payday, before the money has a chance to disappear. Even £50 a week turns into more than £2,500 a year without you thinking about it.

Start small — aim for one month of essentials as an emergency fund, then keep going. Small, automatic, and a little boring is exactly what real financial security looks like.

q2.prompt: You take home £2,000 a month. How much should go to savings and debt?
q2.explanation: 20% of £2,000 is £400 — that's your monthly target for savings and paying down debt.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Garzoni is an educational platform. This policy explains what personal data we collect, why we collect it, and your rights. It is written to comply with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR), the UK Data Protection Act 2018, and where applicable the EU General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) for users in the European Economic Area.

who.title: 1. Who we are
who.body: This policy applies to the Garzoni web app and related services ("Service"). For data protection purposes, the data controller is Garzoni, United Kingdom. If you are in the European Economic Area (EEA), we may act as controller for personal data processed in connection with the Service.

data.title: 2. Data we collect
data.intro: We collect the following categories of data:

account.label: Account data:
account.text: email address, username, and password hash.

profile.label: Profile and preference data:
profile.text: first/last name (if provided), onboarding responses, financial learning preferences, language, reminder settings, and theme settings.

learning.label: Learning and product usage data:
learning.text: lessons viewed, progress, streaks, missions, tool usage events, and feature interactions.

technical.label: Technical data:
technical.text: IP address, device/browser type, operating system, approximate region, timestamps, crash/error logs, and security logs.

cookies.label: Cookie and tracking data:
cookies.text: consent choices, analytics identifiers, and ad/marketing event data where consent is given.

billing.label: Billing metadata:
billing.text: plan, subscription status, and Stripe subscription identifiers. We do not store your full card number.

inputs.label: User-provided finance inputs:
inputs.text: simulated portfolio entries and learning-tool inputs entered by you.

voiceScan.label: Voice and image data (Pro, mobile):
voiceScan.text: audio recordings you submit via the voice tutor (transcribed by OpenAI Whisper and then deleted) and receipt or statement images you upload for scanning (processed by OpenAI Vision and then deleted). Neither audio nor images are stored on our servers beyond the duration of the request.

aiConversations.label: AI tutor conversation history:
aiConversations.text: messages you send to the AI tutor and the responses generated, stored server-side to provide persistent conversation history across sessions and devices.

items.direct: Directly from you (registration, onboarding, settings, tools).
items.automatic: Automatically via app logs, cookies, analytics, and pixels.
items.processors: From processors that support our service (for example Stripe for subscription status).

purposes.title: 4. Why we process your data and legal bases

core.label: Deliver core product features and learning progress

security.label: Keep the platform secure and prevent abuse

comms.label: Send service communications
comms.text: such as account and billing notices (contractual necessity and legitimate interests).

cookies.title: 5. Cookies and similar technologies
cookies.body1: We use strictly necessary cookies for login/session functions and, when you consent, analytics and marketing cookies.
cookies.body2: You can manage consent using our cookie banner and cookie settings. See our <link>Cookie Policy</link> for details.

processors.title: 6. Third-party processors and services
processors.body1: We use third parties to operate the service. Depending on your usage, these may include:

items.cookieConsent: Cookie consent (managed on our site; we do not use third-party consent tools).
items.google: Google Analytics / Google Ads tags (with consent).
items.openai: OpenAI (AI tutor responses, voice transcription, receipt/statement scanning — data processed under OpenAI's API data usage policies).
items.revenuecat: RevenueCat (in-app purchase management and entitlement verification on iOS and Android).
items.customerio: Customer.io (transactional email, push notifications, and AI-generated daily nudges).
items.cloudinary: Cloudinary (media storage for user-uploaded avatars and assets).

processors.body2: These providers process data under contracts and only for approved purposes.

transfers.title: 7. International transfers
transfers.body: Some of our service providers process data outside the UK or the European Economic Area (EEA). Where we do so, we rely on appropriate safeguards: for example UK adequacy regulations, EU adequacy decisions, or standard contractual clauses approved by the UK Secretary of State or the European Commission.

retention.title: 8. Data retention
retention.body: We keep personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy. Our retention periods by data type are:

items.account: Account and profile data (name, email, username, avatar): kept while your account is active. When you delete your account, we erase or anonymise this data within 30 days, unless we must keep certain records to meet legal obligations.
items.activity: Learning progress, XP, streaks and in-app activity: kept while your account is active and deleted when you delete your account.
items.payments: Payment and transaction records: retained for up to 7 years to meet accounting, tax and legal obligations. Payments are processed by our providers (Apple, Google, Stripe, RevenueCat); we do not store full card details.
items.ai: AI tutor conversations and text you submit to AI features: retained for up to 12 months to provide and improve the feature, then deleted or anonymised.
items.media: Camera inputs (receipt and statement scans) and microphone inputs (voice tutor): processed to generate your insights and not retained after processing; any results derived from them are stored under your account until you delete them.
items.logs: Technical, usage and diagnostic data (device identifiers, logs, analytics, crash reports): retained for up to 14 months, after which it is deleted or aggregated into statistics that no longer identify you.
items.support: Support communications: kept for up to 24 months after your request is resolved.

retention.closing: You can request deletion of your data at any time (see Your rights below). After deletion, data may persist in secure backups for a short period before those backups are overwritten on a rolling schedule.

rights.title: 9. Your rights
rights.body: Subject to applicable law (including UK GDPR and, for EEA users, EU GDPR), you may request to:

items.restrict: Restrict or object to certain processing.
items.withdraw: Withdraw consent (where processing is based on consent).
items.portable: Receive a portable copy of data you provided.
items.complaint: Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority: in the UK, the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO); in the EEA, the data protection authority of your country of residence or place of work.

security.title: 10. Security
security.body: We use technical and organizational safeguards designed to protect personal data. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure.

children.body: Garzoni is intended for users aged 18 and over. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 16. In compliance with the UK Online Safety Act and the Children's Code, we take steps to verify that users are adults and to prevent minors from accessing content relating to complex financial products. If you believe a child has created an account or provided personal data, please contact us and we will promptly investigate and delete the data.

If the AI tutor ever appears to suggest a specific investment action, you should disregard it and consult a qualified, regulated financial adviser. AI outputs may contain errors or inaccuracies and should always be verified independently before any financial decision is made.

consumerDuty.title: FCA Consumer Duty
consumerDuty.body: Garzoni is designed in alignment with the principles of the FCA Consumer Duty, which requires platforms to deliver good outcomes for consumers, act in good faith, avoid foreseeable harm, and support customers in achieving their financial objectives. Consistent with this, our tools — including the Portfolio Analyzer, Economic Map, and Market Explorer — are provided exclusively as analytical and educational sandboxes. They are not connected to brokerage accounts, do not execute trades, and should not be treated as investment platforms.

It is written to comply with UK rules (including the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 as amended, and UK GDPR where personal data is processed) and with EU rules on cookies and similar technologies (the ePrivacy Directive and the General Data Protection Regulation where applicable).

what.title: 1. What cookies are
what.body: Cookies are small text files placed on your device when you visit a website. They help with login, security, analytics, and service performance.

sessionPersistent.title: 2. Session and persistent cookies
sessionPersistent.sessionBody: Session cookies let the site recognise and link your actions during a single browsing session. They are typically used for purposes such as remembering what you put in a basket while you browse. Session cookies often store an identifier so you can move from page to page without re-entering your username, password, etc. They last only for that session and are deleted when you close the browser or app.
sessionPersistent.persistentBody: Persistent cookies are stored across sessions and can remember your preferences or actions on a site (or across sites)—for example language, theme, menu preferences, or favourite pages. We use them only where you have consented or where they are strictly necessary for the service you requested.

necessary.label: Strictly necessary cookies:
necessary.text: required for core functionality such as login, session handling, and security.

analytics.label: Analytics cookies:
analytics.text: help us understand usage and improve product experience.

marketing.label: Marketing cookies:
marketing.text: measure campaign performance and ad interactions, where consent is provided.

In the EEA, the ePrivacy rules and national implementations impose similar requirements. Consent must be informed, specific, and freely given. We do not set non-essential cookies until you have given your consent.

consent.title: 5. Managing your consent
